protocol.topic:
Comparative Performance of Commercial Deep Learning Systems for Referable Diabetic Retinopathy Screening: Real-World Deployment-Context Bayesian Arm-Based Network Meta-Analysis

Population: People undergoing referable diabetic retinopathy (rDR) screening in defined real-world deployment contexts — primary-care community, national screening programs, referral / specialty clinics, regulatory-pivotal trials.

Intervention / Index test: Any commercially available or regulator-approved (FDA, CE, NMPA, HSA, TGA, MHRA) deep-learning automated retinal image analysis system (ARIAS), applied to fundus photography. Examples include IDx-DR, EyeArt, Selena+, RetCAD, OphtAI, Medios AI, Remidio, Retmarker, RetinaLyze, MONA, NEC, DRISTi, Verily.

Comparator: Implicit through the arm-based network — each ARIAS contributes single-arm DTA evidence; system / camera / region / prevalence enter as meta-regression covariates. Originally restricted to within-study head-to-head comparisons of ≥2 commercial systems in the same population (v1 / v2, rejected at AAO Ophthalmology). Pivoted 2026-05-15 to admit single-arm regulator-approved studies to recover meta-regression power (k/p ≈ 1.3 at k=12 with 9 covariates was structurally underpowered; τ_specificity = 1.40 on logit scale, no covariate reached significance).

Outcomes:
  Primary  — Patient-level sensitivity and specificity for rDR by deployment context, pooled in a Bayesian bivariate arm-based NMA (Nyaga / Owen framework).
  Secondary — Eye-level sensitivity / specificity; screen-positive rate; referral burden; (where reported) interval / progression-to-VTDR cancers.

Three eligibility filters (locked 2026-05-15):
  F1  Image modality = fundus photography only (exclude OCT / OCTA / UWF-only / smartphone-without-fundus-attachment).
  F2  Reference outcome = referable DR (rDR) only (exclude all-grade DR, vision-threatening DR alone, diabetic macular edema alone).
  F3  System = commercially available / regulator-approved (exclude pure research prototypes; Gulshan / Gargeya / Ting research code excluded unless productised).

Design: Bayesian hierarchical bivariate Network Meta-Analysis (DTA). Node = deployment context. System / vendor demoted from node to meta-regression covariate (DR analog of the keratoconus modality-as-node pivot).

Registration: INPLASY202620069. Amendment 2 (H2H → arm-based scope change) pending circulation to co-authors before any analysis re-run.

Search dates: inception to 2026-01-29 (frozen). Languages: English. Databases: PubMed (E-utilities API), Embase (Elsevier portal manual export), ClinicalTrials.gov (manual + API). Raw counts: 1,847 / 2,114 / 187 = 4,148 → 3,105 dedup → 706 dual-screened.

Evidence base for arm-based pivot: harvested from two adjacent sibling SR/MAs by the same author —
  • Oph MA/Certified/ (regulator-certified DR AI systems, published in npj Digital Medicine 2025: s41746-025-01717-9)
  • Oph MA/Prospective/ (prospective DR AI evaluations, submitted)
plus the existing Oph MA/Network/ H2H pool. Working k = 119 manifest rows (117 PDFs on disk) after harvest and dedup, pending PDF triage on the unclear F3 subset.

Co-author team: Ting-Wei Wang (first / submitting), Wei-Chieh Fang, Wei-Ting Luo, Yu-Kang Tu (methodological pre-vet pending), Yu-Te Wu, Yu-Bai Chou (corresponding).

Prior submission history: AAO Ophthalmology v1 2026-02-26, v2 2026-03-08 (rejected). Target journal v3 pending Dr. Chou's decision (npj Digital Medicine leaning; JAMA Ophthalmology / Translational Vision Science & Technology / British Journal of Ophthalmology as fallbacks).

Salami-slicing disclosure: included-study set overlaps with the published Certified and submitted Prospective sibling papers. Cover letter and Methods must justify the methodological distinction explicitly (BMJ-vs-Lancet template applies):
  Axis             Certified           Prospective         New arm-based DR NMA
  Model            pooled DTA          pooled DTA          Bayesian arm-based bivariate NMA
  Evidence base    certified-only      prospective-only    union, dedup'd post-filter
  Headline         "are certified      "prospective        "deployment-context landscape,
                   AI systems          real-world          system as covariate"
                   accurate?"          performance?"

rows.Notes: Retrospective consecutive screening cohort, 3 masked graders with majority consensus; flow concern — split grader teams (Polish vs Indian), no adjudication, 107 excluded for IDx-DR-defined quality.

Retrospective 101,710 consecutive encounters across 404 clinics; single EyePACS grader (no per-case adjudication) — authors flag 'lack of adjudicated multiple reader grading' as a limitation; validation data independent from training.
Consecutive T2DM at Hoorn DCS; IDx-DR 2.0 locked, masked to 3-expert adjudicated reference; but only 898/1415 (63.5%) analysed due to image-quality exclusions — flow/timing High.
Consecutive NDESP recruitment, locked EyeArt v2.1.0, vendor masked; reference standard is NDESP grading where 'graders are mostly non-medical personnel' — not retinal-specialist as PICO requires.
Retrospective; post-hoc operating point 'chosen such that sensitivity and specificity were approximately equal'; ~90% single-grader reference; ICDR/Scottish grading mismatch flagged by authors.
Retrospective; primary reference was a single optometrist (paper admits 'Each image was graded by only 1 optometrist'), not ophthalmologist; 80/260 (30.8%) excluded as ungradable.
Tertiary-referral pilot (n=54) excluding DMO — part of referable DR target; authors admit sample 'not representative of the general population'; reference grader masking/adjudication not described.
Prospective interventional cohort in Thai national DR screening; CE-marked v2 DLS; 3-specialist adjudication masked to DLS; CONSORT-AI followed; no explicit statement on training-set overlap.

Prospective 7-hospital validation with masked 2-grader+adjudicator reference; authors acknowledge 'hospital settings...does not align with community screening' — applicability mismatch with rDR screening PICO.

First 106 consecutive screening patients, but 'further 50 patients were evaluated in the hospital's outpatient eye clinic' to enrich severe DR — distorts screening prevalence; adjudication between 2 graders not described.
Retrospective consecutive enrollment (550 subjects), 3 masked expert graders with senior-retina adjudication, locked Medios AI-DR on Armenian population 'unseen during training'; STARD-style flow.
Retrospective community screening with locked EyeArt v2.0; two masked graders with expert adjudication ('did not know any information about...EyeArt'); 101/684 patients excluded.
Differential reference: DRB adjudicated only the 420 discordant cases while 734 concordant cases used GO+RS+AI agreement; outcome is any DR, not specifically referable DR.
Multicentre prospective validation across 5 Spanish hospitals; 3 masked retina specialists as reference; 115/945 (12%) excluded for missing/no-consensus DR scores — flow incompletely reported.
Random recruitment from Retisalud screening, locked EyeArt 2.1.0 externally validated; RoB high for reference standard — 'reference standard relied on grading by a single ophthalmologist.'
Retrospective validation of FDA-approved EyeArt on local Jalisco dataset 'unseen by both systems'; 3-ophthalmologist majority reference; enrollment method and AI-grader masking not stated.

Prospective consecutive inpatients at tertiary diabetes center (age 8-92, biased toward referred/sicker cases); locked commercial IDx-DR; single ophthalmologist reference, 'no second or third grader' for adjudication.

Consecutive adults with prospective recruitment and pre-specified thresholds, but reference standard was a single retinal specialist with no adjudication, and 12.8% were excluded with differential characteristics (older, longer diabetes dur

Retrospective Messidor-2 public dataset (high-quality images, not screening-representative); IDx-DR X2.1 locked, not trained on Messidor-2; 3-expert adjudicated reference; pre-specified high-sensitivity set points.
Prospective consecutive recruitment in diabetes outpatient clinic with locked commercial AI versions; reference = single ophthalmologist with no adjudication or explicit masking (High RoB reference).
Retrospective consecutive enrollment with blinded AI vs ophthalmologist; authors note 'main limitation is the use of only one ophthalmologist as a human grader' — single-grader reference standard.

Pre-registered (NCT04805541) consecutive endocrinology cohort, 3-specialist masked consensus on 4-widefield images, version-locked EyeCheckup; but training used same-site Akdeniz images — no explicit test/train separation.

Retrospective; consecutive DM patients but 'all images analyzed in this study were taken from encounters deemed as sufficient by the IDx-DR quality check', biasing flow and selection; split Polish/Indian grader teams limit reference consist
Retrospective consecutive 811 diabetic-clinic patients in Poland; 3 graders/side masked to AI, consensus reference; commercial locked AI (IDx-DR, Medios); STARD diagram presented.

Retrospective consecutive screening cohort (750 pts), 3 masked expert graders with majority consensus; MONA DR v1.0.0 trained on EyePACS (US) with patient-level split, tested externally on Polish screening data.

Retrospective non-representative sample (60 rDR+ / 110 rDR-) with ungradable images excluded; reference was a single ophthalmologist with 'basic experience' — authors themselves flag selection bias and weak ground truth.
Prospective evaluation of locked CE-marked EyeArt v2.1.0 on 30,405 consecutive UK DESP episodes; multi-grader NHS protocol with arbitration as reference; AI masked to human grade.
Consecutive prospective enrollment, locked Medios NM App V.2.0 read masked; reference was a single 'field grader' (ophthalmic technician), not an ophthalmologist/retinal specialist — PICO mismatch.
Tertiary retina-clinic convenience sample (RWDR 73.9%) — not a screening cohort; single retina-specialist reference; EyeArt v2.0 trained on traditional, not smartphone, images.
Retrospective consecutive cohort; FDA-locked IDx-DR vs single ophthalmologist/optometrist overread 'not masked to the original grading, which may have introduced bias'.

Consecutive DESP screening cohort with RetCAD v2.1.0 (locked, externally trained: 'None of the images used in this study were used to train'); reference is DESP manual grade, not retinal-specialist adjudication.

Prospective single-center Genoa cohort May-Sep 2019, EyeArt v2.0 + IDx-DR vs two masked retina specialists with consensus; enrollment described as 'recruited or referred' — consecutiveness not stated.

Consecutive enrollment with locked CE-marked Retmarker (trained in Portugal 2015/2018) validated in Italian cohort; key limitation is single ophthalmologist grader — 'use of only one ophthalmologist as human grader'.

Consecutive prospective enrollment with locked commercial AI, but 'Greifswald modification' threshold derived post-hoc via Youden Index on same test set and reference was single ophthalmologist per patient.
Consecutive screening at tertiary eye hospital; 418/2700 'insufficient quality' images excluded and grader masking to IDx-DR output not stated; IDx-DR v2.3 locked, external to training.

rows.Notes: All consecutive NEL DESP encounters (2021-2022) processed by 8 CE-marked ARIAS; reference = up to 3 masked NHS graders; 'this real-life dataset...has not been used to develop or train any ARIAS'.

Prospective consecutive enrollment, 5 masked retina specialists with majority adjudication; explicit statement that 'images used for training and internal validation of the AI do not overlap with those captured for the SMART study.'
Consecutive enrollment but non-diseased arm down-sampled by random selection (804→657) creating artificial case mix; 3 masked graders with adjudication; THEIA trained on same Auckland DHB population.
Prospective multicenter consecutive enrollment, masked 2-grader ZIRC adjudication, pre-specified threshold, STARD-followed; training/validation source overlap not explicitly excluded.

Consecutive OPD diabetic patients; two masked VR specialists with adjudication as ground truth; commercial Medios AI; mydriatic 3-field imaging at tertiary diabetes centre limits screening applicability.
Enriched with '50 patients with more severe DR' on top of 106 consecutive screenees (two-gate); target was any-DR vs non-DR, not referable DR per PICO.

Consecutive OPD enrollment at tertiary diabetes center with 3-field mydriatic imaging; two masked VR specialists adjudicated (κ=0.89); training set (EyePACS/camps) distinct from test site but overlap not explicitly excluded.
Consecutive T2DM screening cohort; IDx-DR 2.0 with pre-specified thresholds masked to 3 adjudicated retinal specialists; ~35% excluded for image quality, no per-patient flow detail.

20258 consecutive NHS DESP patients; reference = accredited screening graders (not retinal specialists) with Doheny arbitration only on discrepancies + random subset (differential verification); vendors given 2500 Homerton images to 'optimi

Retrospective external validation in Indigenous Australians using consecutive images, CE-marked DLS with thresholds 'locked prior to the commencement of this study,' 3-person adjudicated reference, STARD-reported.
Retrospective NTUH-only split; threshold chosen at 'optimal operating point' on the validation set (post-hoc); 2-grader + senior retina adjudication reference standard; no external validation.
Consecutive real-world DR screening with locked RetCAD v2.0.2; reference standard was a single general ophthalmologist — authors acknowledge this as 'primary limitation'.

Consecutive recruitment with masked 2+1 adjudication and locked EyeArt v2.1, but ambulatory-clinic Caucasian-only sample with R2 prevalence 'higher than what typically reported in a screening programme' limits applicability.

Locked algorithms masked to double-arbitrated retina-specialist reference; but 94.68% male veterans (applicability) and referable-DR threshold = any DR (ICDR 1-4), not mtmDR; retrospective 2006-2018 images.

Retrospective case-enriched sample of patients with 'pre-existing diagnosis of DR (any) or AMD (any)'—authors concede 'a biased sample'; not a screening cohort, so selection and applicability are High.

Case-enriched 'random selection of 600 images' from pre-graded clinical pool (not consecutive DM screening); single ophthalmologist RS without adjudication; post-hoc 'optimal operating point' selected on ROC.
Consecutive 503 pts at tertiary diabetes clinic; fundoscopy by single ophthalmologist (1 of 4) 'ohne Kenntnis des Ergebnisses' der IDx-DR — no multi-grader adjudication; age range 9-92 (incl. peds).

Cross-camera validation of VeriSee DR on images pre-filtered as 'gradable' by one ophthalmologist; convenience sample from 3 clinics, not consecutive screening cohort; 3-grader majority vote reference.
Prospective GP-based recruitment with locked EyeArt v2.1.0; double-grading with adjudication masked to AI; small N=75 and only 6 DED cases limit precision but methodology is sound.
Retrospective convenience sample of 62 patients (32% denied T2DM, 23% unknown); single off-site retina specialist as reference; small N=124 eyes from community screening.
Preregistered prospective multicenter pivotal trial of locked EyeArt v2.1.0; FPRC ETDRS reference by 2 masked graders + adjudication; enrichment corrected; STARD-compliant.
Post-hoc analysis of 135 consecutive diabetic patients at tertiary eye hospital (not screening setting); 63/233 eyes excluded as ungradable; Medios AI vs 2-expert consensus + adjudication, masked.
Prospective multicenter pivotal trial; FDA-cleared locked EyeArt; 2 masked WFPRC graders with adjudication on 4-wide-field ETDRS stereo as reference; STARD chart reported.
Convenience recruitment via ads+GP referrals (not consecutive); MC reference included non-specialist graders without certified reading centre; CLARUS camera not yet validated for EyeArt v2.1.0.

Single-day convenience pilot of 33 minority women (64 eyes, only 12 DR+); two retina specialists graded but adjudication/masking unspecified; locked EyeArt v2.1.0 (CE-marked), EyeNuk co-author conflict.

Balanced case-control sampling (52 rDR + 52 randomly selected non-rDR 'primarily myopia') = high selection RoB; in-house EfficientNet-B4, not commercial/regulator-approved AI, so index-test applicability is high.

Prospective 3-center double-masked trial with 3-grader+PI consensus reference, but sample engineered to ~70% positives ('positive data in this study accounted for 68.14%'), inflating prevalence vs real screening.

Differential verification: adjudication only for disagreement cases plus 5% of agreement cases — 'may overestimate the accuracy of both deep learning and human graders'; Google research algorithm, not yet regulator-approved.
Consecutive T2D cohort, locked EyeArt v3.0.0, STARD-adherent and blinded, but reference was a single retinal specialist with no adjudication and analytic cohort restricted to gradable eyes.
Retrospective 200-image set; CSIRO research software (not commercial/regulator-approved); thresholds derived post-hoc via Youden's index — 'optimal cutoffs were derived from the Youden's index'.

Prospective house-to-house SMART India cohort; SERI-trained, Zeiss VISUHEALTH-AI v1.8 (locked) externally validated on non-mydriatic handheld images; 2-grader+arbitration reference masked to AI; no TRIPOD-AI.

Case-control selection of 50 referable/50 nonreferable hospital images (mostly advanced DR) — non-commercial in-house ARIA, EyePACS-trained, Mexican-hospital tested; 3-specialist majority gold standard.
Consecutive T2DM screening at VGHTC with TFDA-approved VeriSee vs 3 masked ophthalmologists (adjudicated); ~30-35% poor-quality images excluded, no training-overlap statement.
In-house MIRA CNN (only SAFE CREATIVE copyright code, not FDA/CE) — mismatches PICO's 'commercial/regulator-approved'; retrospective testing; 4 masked retina experts but no adjudication described.

Retrospective VA validation of 7 locked commercial AI algorithms vs double-masked arbitrated expert grading; 'None of the images had been used previously to train' algorithms; cohort 94.68% male veterans limits applicability.

Retrospective measurement-comparison in 20,258 'consecutive diabetic patients' at NHS DESP; manual grade modified by masked reading-centre arbitration as reference; locked CE-marked ARIAS versions; pre-TRIPOD-AI.

Prospective public-health screening, masked dual-grader RS with senior adjudication, STARD-reported; AI retrained between phases but 'did not undergo additional training during the implementation period.'
Consecutive enrollment at 4 Rwandan diabetes clinics with prospective AI screening (Cybersight AI), but reference was a single UK NHS-certified grader, not ≥2 adjudicated experts.

Prospective single-center study using CE-marked RetCAD vs external Reading Center (NHS DESP); RC grader number/masking not specified, and ICDR↔NHS scale mapping introduces reference-standard uncertainty.

Consecutive primary-care sampling with pre-specified threshold (0.0166), but reference was a single teleophthalmologist — authors concede 'assess each case by more than one physician' is needed; retrospective design.

manuscript.abstract_md:
# Abstract

**Background.** Multiple commercial deep-learning artificial intelligence (AI) systems are now
regulator-cleared for referable diabetic retinopathy (rDR) screening on fundus photographs,
but their head-to-head comparative diagnostic accuracy has not been quantified in a unified
framework.

**Methods.** We conducted a Bayesian bivariate hierarchical network meta-analysis (NMA) of
diagnostic test accuracy (DTA) data following PRISMA-DTA. Studies were identified through
49 full-text records harmonised from prospective and certified-AI source pools.
After applying restricted eligibility (commercial regulator-approved AI on fundus images,
patient-wise or exam-wise reporting only, complete 2×2 cells), 79 arms across
43 studies and 21 commercial AI systems were included in the bivariate
JAGS NMA (50 000 iterations × 3 chains after 10 000 burn-in). IDx-DR served as the reference
node. We pre-screened nine covariates (prevalence, healthcare setting, economic tier, camera
type, vendor involvement, dilation, diagnostic criteria, etc.) for meta-regression effects.
Heterogeneity was quantified by between-study τ on the logit scale and I². Publication bias
was assessed by Deeks' regression. Certainty of evidence was rated using GRADE for DTA;
risk of bias was assessed with QUADAS-3.

**Results.** Pooled sensitivity for IDx-DR was 0.97
(95 % CrI 0.94–0.99) and specificity
0.81 (0.73–0.88). EyeArt
sensitivity was 0.97 (0.93–0.99)
and specificity 0.81 (0.71–0.89).
Between-study heterogeneity was substantial (τ-sensitivity 0.93, τ-specificity
0.91; I² 98.8% / 100.0%). Meta-regression identified
**prevalence, cameratype as significant moderator(s)**. Funnel-plot
asymmetry was present (Deeks' P = 0.007). On the joint SUCRA ranking the top systems were
THEIA, LuxIA, and Baidu DR. Certainty of
evidence was HIGH for 1 system, MODERATE for 3, LOW for 8, and VERY LOW for 9 — the latter
all driven by single-arm sparse-evidence concerns.

**Conclusions.** Among regulator-approved commercial DR AI systems, IDx-DR (FDA) and EyeArt
(FDA, CE) currently offer the most robust evidence for primary-care rDR screening, while
many newer systems remain supported by single-cohort validations. Sensitivity is acceptable
across most systems (>0.85 posterior mean) but specificity varies widely and is highly
camera- and prevalence-dependent. Deployment decisions should account for residual
heterogeneity and limited evidence base for newer entrants.

**Keywords:** diabetic retinopathy, artificial intelligence, deep learning, network
meta-analysis, sensitivity, specificity, screening, fundus photography.

# Results

## Study selection and characteristics

The harmonised evidence pool comprised 49 eligible full-text records.
After applying the restricted eligibility criteria — commercial regulator-approved AI on
fundus images, patient-wise or exam-wise reporting, complete 2 × 2 cells — 79 arms
across 43 studies covering 21 unique AI systems were retained for
quantitative synthesis (Figure 1, network plot).

Of the 43 included studies, only **10**
provided direct head-to-head comparisons of two or more AI systems on the same image
cohort; the remainder contributed single-arm validations. The most-compared pair was
**IDx-DR ↔ RetCAD** (3 studies).

## Pooled diagnostic performance

Across all 21 commercial systems, posterior mean sensitivity ranged from
0.78 to 1.00, and posterior mean
specificity from 0.53 to 0.97
(Table 1, Figure 2 forest). The reference system IDx-DR achieved sensitivity
0.97 (95 % CrI 0.94–0.99)
and specificity 0.81
(0.73–0.88). EyeArt achieved sensitivity
0.97 (0.93–0.99) and
specificity 0.81
(0.71–0.89). On the HSROC plane (Figure 3) most
systems cluster in the high-sensitivity / moderate-specificity region appropriate for
screening.

## Ranking (SUCRA)

Joint Sens × Spec SUCRA ranking placed the top five systems as:

| Rank | AI system | SUCRA Sens | SUCRA Spec |
|---:|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | THEIA | 0.99 | 0.88 |
| 2 | LuxIA | 0.68 | 0.66 |
| 3 | Baidu DR | 0.56 | 0.69 |
| 4 | RAIS-DR | 0.39 | 0.84 |
| 5 | Google ARDA | 0.46 | 0.69 |


(See Figure 4 SUCRA 2D scatter and Supplementary Figure S2 for cumulative ranking
probabilities.)

## Heterogeneity, covariates, and publication bias

Between-study heterogeneity was substantial: τ-sensitivity 0.93 and
τ-specificity 0.91 on the logit scale (corresponding I² 98.8 % and
100.0 %; Supplementary Table ST1). Meta-regression on the pre-specified
covariates identified **prevalence, cameratype**
as influencing diagnostic accuracy (95 % CrI excluding zero; Supplementary Table ST2).
All other covariates (economical, healthcare, vendor, dilation, diagnostic criteria) showed no significant
association. Funnel-plot asymmetry was significant (Deeks' regression P = 0.007;
Supplementary Figure S3), suggesting either selective reporting or genuine between-study
heterogeneity in true accuracy.
